title: Regex Apply Mode (Only Display / Only Prompt / Both) undocumented — the single most important regex control
reality: docs/extending/regex-scripts.md documents Apply Mode in Advanced Options, separate from Placement. Only Display changes only on-screen text (saved message and future model context unchanged); Only Prompt changes only what the model receives (display and saved message unchanged); Both changes each. A NEW SCRIPT STARTS ON 'Only Display'. Critical exception: a User Input script set to Only Display or Both rewrites the message right before sending, so it changes what is actually saved and sent — there is no display-only mode for outgoing user messages. references/custom-tools.md documents none of this.
fix: Add an Apply Mode subsection to the Regex Scripts section of references/custom-tools.md, including the Only Display default and the user-input exception. HIGH severity: the default means a user following the skill's current advice writes a script that appears to do nothing to the model, and the user-input exception is a genuine data-mutating footgun.

title: Regex Placement and Execution Order/Depth Range undocumented
reality: docs/extending/regex-scripts.md documents Placement (AI Output vs User Input) and, under Advanced Options, Execution Order (lower runs first; new scripts start at 0 and the app assigns the next free number on save to avoid collisions; rows are drag-reorderable) and Depth Range (Min/Max counting BACKWARD from the newest message, which is depth 0; leave both empty to run at any depth; saving is blocked if min > max).
fix: Document Placement, Execution Order, and Depth Range in references/custom-tools.md, mapping them to the schema fields placement, order, minDepth, maxDepth from pass A. The depth-0-is-newest convention and the min>max save block are both concrete and easy to get wrong.

title: Reserved built-in tool names not listed
reality: docs/extending/custom-tools.md 'Reserved names' states a custom tool name cannot match a built-in: roll_dice, update_game_state, set_expression, trigger_event, search_lorebook, web_search, update_about_me, among others. Saving one produces '"your_name" is a reserved built-in tool name.' Two custom tools also cannot share a name. references/custom-tools.md does not list the reserved set.
fix: Add the reserved names to references/custom-tools.md next to the existing snake_case naming rule. The skill already tells users to name tools in lowercase snake_case; the reserved list is the other half of that constraint and prevents a confusing save failure.

title: Attaching tools to an agent is a documented first-class flow
reality: docs/extending/custom-tools.md has a dedicated 'Attaching tools to an agent' section, and 'Turning on tool use for a chat' explains that Enable Tool Use with no tools listed grants access to ALL globally enabled tools (built-ins plus every enabled custom tool), while adding specific tools narrows the set. references/custom-tools.md now covers the all-vs-narrowed rule but not the agent-attachment flow in its own right.
fix: Add an 'Attaching tools to an agent' note to references/custom-tools.md, cross-linked from references/agents.md's tool-using-agents section, which currently approaches the same relationship from only one side.

title: Include hidden chat context has its own documented section
reality: docs/extending/custom-tools.md dedicates a section to 'Include hidden chat context', the setting the v2.4.0 import hardening forcibly disables on imported webhooks. references/custom-tools.md names includeHiddenContext in the schema and in the import-security note but never explains what the context actually contains or when enabling it is legitimate.
fix: Expand includeHiddenContext coverage in references/custom-tools.md: what it exposes, why it is the reason imported webhooks are force-disabled, and when a self-authored tool genuinely needs it.
